tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] USER 2026-08-26: '약을 들면 안 보여 보이게' - when she holds the medicine she cannot see it. The held-tool viewmodel is not visible, and she followed up with the reason it matters: '해줘 그래야 흔들리는 게 보이지' - do it, so the sloshing can be seen.
tasks.note: THIS IS UPSTREAM OF #1025 AND SHE SAID SO HERSELF: an invisible liquid can slosh all it likes and nobody sees it. Everything an979 is building sits behind this. Dispatched with hypotheses explicitly labelled as MINE and not a diagnosis, since my hypotheses were wrong several times today: not rendered at all (layer / camera culling mask / active state); inside the near plane or off-screen; too small; TOO DARK - which is a live candidate because the reception body was exactly that today, present and rendering and reading only as a silhouette in a dim room; or a HideHeadFromSelf-style self-hiding rule reaching the viewmodel. ANSWER WITH THE A/B GATE, same-frame plus grid cells: if the pixels do not change with the viewmodel hidden it is not being drawn; if they DO change and she still cannot see it, that is CONTRAST, not existence - and those two are fixed in completely different places. If contrast, the standing rule holds: fix it on the object, never by lifting the room. an979's own finding that VM_Cup is a blue CUBE feeds straight into this - a dark blue cube disappears in a dark room. || ANSWERED 2026-08-26T21:49:28 by ps981, measurement only, probe reverted, no code touched. IT IS A POSITION BUG - not existence, not contrast. ViewModelAnchor sits at camera-local (0.46, -0.42, 0.55) with FOV 70, putting its centre at VIEWPORT Y = -0.045, BELOW THE FRAME. The Cup is ~28% on screen, hugging the bottom edge. EXISTENCE IS FINE: every slot instantiates exactly one renderer, nothing culled or inactive, no layer/mask problem. CONTRAST IS FINE AND THIS IS THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE SENT SOMEONE THE WRONG WAY: viewmodel luminance 102-175 against background 44, MICHELSON 0.39-0.60 - the dark lobby is not the cause here, and my own hypothesis list had it as a live candidate. TWO CROSS-CHECKS: all eight slots change only 0.216-0.582% of the frame, BELOW the 2% floor the shared A/B gate uses, so the standard gate would have correctly failed all eight; and the arithmetic agrees with the pixels to three decimals (half-height 0.3851, 0.5 + 0.5*(-0.42/0.3851) = -0.0453 against a measured -0.045). CONSEQUENCE FOR #1025 THAT ps981 SPOTTED AND I HAD NOT: the visible 28% IS THE CUP'S TOP RIM, roughly where a liquid surface would sit - and there is NO ROOM ABOVE IT for the surface to move into. So the anchor decides how much slosh can be seen at all, and tuning the slosh against the current anchor would be tuning something nobody can see. || CLOSED 2026-08-30: verified in main by merge-base (68c84e1 is an ancestor of da02a06). tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] Camera.main returns NULL during the QA capture sequence, because a preceding staged shot leaves the room camera DISABLED and Camera.main only returns ENABLED cameras. Anything reaching for Camera.main inside that sequence hits the same thing.
tasks.note: Incidental finding by ps981 while measuring #1036 - their first attempt got null. THIS IS THE #986 MECHANISM FROM A THIRD DIRECTION. #986 was Billboard caching Camera.main and surviving the camera being disabled, because a DISABLED Unity component is not == null. Here the inverse: Camera.main SKIPS disabled cameras, so code that expects it to find the room camera gets nothing. Same underlying fact - QACaptureDriver disables the room camera - producing opposite failures depending on whether you cached or queried. Worth a single fix at the source rather than three workarounds: either the capture sequence restores camera state between shots, or callers inside it are handed the camera explicitly instead of asking a global.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] THE DAY'S CONCLUSION: the strongest evidence today came from the user's own sentence, not from any instrument. No probe could have produced it.

The log showed WHERE her time went and could never have shown WHY. Same shape across the whole day: '접수가 안돼' was a frozen window nobody's suite could see; '안 움직여 중간에' was a GAME OVER panel that existed and was hidden; '사람들이' - plural - was the word the orchestrator read past and bd986 did not; '약을 들면 안 보여' was an anchor 0.045 below the viewport that eight green suites had never asked about; and '나는 비밀요원이라니깐' explained a check-in count that two sessions could not choose an explanation for. FIVE TIMES A TEN-YEAR-OLD'S SENTENCE WAS THE MEASUREMENT. The instruments were not wrong to build - each one closed the question the sentence opened, and #1036 was answered in one pass because ps981 had a gate to point at it. But the ORDER is the lesson: she says what is wrong, the instrument says why, and no amount of instrument produces the first half.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] WAVE RULE, and it is the inverse of everything else caught today: A TRUE NUMBER THAT ANSWERS A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED. Following it leads you to fix a real, measurable, irrelevant problem - and the user's complaint survives the fix.
tasks.note: bd986's formulation at the close of #1036. Every other defect this wave was an instrument returning GREEN over the question it was built to answer; this is an instrument returning TRUE over a DIFFERENT question. Concretely: the held cup was never hard to see - luminance 102-175 against a background of 44, Michelson 0.39-0.60 - it was in the WRONG PLACE, 0.045 below the viewport. WHAT MADE THE TRAP LIVE: this room had burned the project on darkness TWICE the same day (#972's greeter, and the orchestrator describing the reception body as 'near-silhouetted'), so a third darkness explanation would have felt well-supported. Anyone chasing it would have found a genuine contrast issue, fixed it properly, and she still could not see her cup. SAME LINEAGE AS THE LICENCE STRING: a string present in 110 of 110 logs was used to name a cause; it was true and irrelevant, and the wrapper printed a confident wrong diagnosis from it. THE DEFENCE IS THE SAME IN BOTH CASES: before acting on a measurement, state which question it answers and check that it is the question that was asked. CREDIT AS bd986 INSISTED IT BE RECORDED: viewModel=yes on all eight was the log line doing its job on its first run, not insight; it deleted one of four candidates, and ps981's anchor arithmetic is what closed it.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] OUR TEST RUNS DELETE HER SAVE FILE. Eight call sites call SaveSystem.Delete() against the LIVE path; the editor and her build share persistentDataPath (same company/product). M6FixTest is in the ordinary sweep, so a ROUTINE SWEEP WIPES HER PROGRESS. Her file was watched vanishing between 21:47 and 21:50.
tasks.note: ALL SWEEPS STOPPED wave-wide until this lands and is verified. Orchestrator backed her save up first: ~/animal-hospital-playtest/save-backups/save-215312.json (403 bytes, selectedJob=intern, purchasedJobs=['intern'], bestShift=1) - the loss so far is small because the game recreates a fresh file and her progress was one shift, but the defect is not small. WHY IT OUTRANKS EVERYTHING CAUGHT TODAY: every other defect this wave was an instrument LYING TO US; this one DESTROYS HER DATA. And it fires on an ordinary sweep, so nobody knows how many of the dozens run today wiped her file. CHECK WHETHER THIS IS A RECURRENCE - the session summary from this morning records a 'save-wipe blocker' closed end-to-end with a human press; if it is the same root, what was fixed then and why it came back decides the shape of this fix. FIX THE CAUSE, NOT THE SYMPTOM: the symptom is that tests delete the save, the CAUSE is that tests can SEE the live path, so patching eight call sites is a workaround and a ninth gets added tomorrow. Proposed direction (not an instruction): give SaveSystem an injectable root and point tests at a temp path so they CANNOT REACH the live file - #1017's shape, fix the predicate rather than carve exemptions - plus a guard that fails loudly if a live-path Delete() is called from a test context, which should then never fire. #1013 applies: prove the guard bites for the right reason, name which assertion went red, AND DO NOT RUN THAT NEGATIVE CONTROL AGAINST HER REAL SAVE. A pre-sweep auto-backup is a belt and comes SECOND; having a backup is not permission to delete. || SCOPE ENLARGED 2026-08-26T21:55:56 by sp977, and it changes the fix. TEN call sites, not eight: one editor suite (M6FixTest, Delete TWICE), SEVEN play-mode QA probes (HotbarProbe, LobbyVisibilityProbe, InteractProbe, MimicProbe, EmptyHandProbe, SkinProbe, QACaptureDriver) and MainMenuController:294 which is presumably a legitimate in-game path. THE SECOND PATH IS QUIETER AND WORSE: QACaptureDriver.cs:43 is NOT in the sweep and fires on EVERY CAPTURE RUN - sp977 has 16 capture logs today - so it is not only 'an ordinary sweep wipes her progress', AN ORDINARY CAPTURE DOES TOO, and the double-run rule we imposed for the cold-shader-cache DOUBLES THE DAMAGE. The rule that protects the captures doubled the deletions. sp977 counted their own share unprompted: eleven full sweeps x two Delete calls = about 22 deletions from sweeps alone, by them; and having MEASURED that the 21:47-21:50 deletion was not theirs (empty window across their logs) they wrote 'that is the least interesting fact here - the ones nobody watched were mine'. FIX SHAPE, from their observation: the DETERMINISTIC-BOOT INTENT IS LEGITIMATE AND SHOULD SURVIVE; what is wrong is the SCOPE - the tests want a clean save FOR THE RUN, not the destruction of the file at that path. So redirect the path in test/probe context rather than removing the Delete calls, plus a guard that FAILS if the live save path is ever the target. || THIRD WIDENING 2026-08-26T21:59:27 AND IT FIXES THE FIX'S SHAPE. It is 57 call sites of SaveSystem.Save|Load|Delete|HasSave across the tree; DELETE IS ONLY 10 OF THEM. TWELVE sites explicitly pass SaveSystem.DefaultPath and NEVER CALL Delete() - they destroy her save, HER BACKUP (.bak) and her temp without a single Delete call, taking out the very .bak recovery path M4aSelfTest exists to protect. A Delete-only fix touches NONE of those twelve. And it is ELEVEN suites, not M6FixTest alone; an ordinary sweep runs most of them, so the sweep has been destroying her save from about eleven directions. VERIFICATION CONDITION FOLLOWS: grep for DefaultPath, not for Delete( - that is where the twelve hide. THE CORRECT PATTERN IS ALREADY IN THE REPO: M4aSelfTest uses Application.temporaryCachePath and never persistentDataPath, exercising save/load/corruption/.bak without touching her file. So this is not a new design - it is 'make the other eleven look like M4aSelfTest', with a working reference to copy. AND THAT IS #1041 FROM THE OTHER SIDE: a good idea spread without its precondition, while the CORRECT idea sat in one file and was not copied. Both forms lived in the same repo and the wrong one spread. || FIX VERIFIED 2026-08-26T22:03:25, 8/8, and HER FILE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after - shasum f7eebc9b61ef74f8068fc24e5d80af2e9634751c, 403 bytes, mtime 21:52:16, confirmed INDEPENDENTLY by bd986 and by the orchestrator against a pre-run backup. TWO LAYERS: (1) diagnostic runs - editor, batchmode, or a probe flag - get their own root under temporaryCachePath so tests CANNOT REACH the live file; DefaultPath resolved to /var/folders/.../T/AnimalHospital/AnimalHospital/diagnostic-save/save.json. (2) Delete() REFUSES a live path unless playerInitiated:true, which only MainMenuController.NewGame passes - SO AN ELEVENTH CALL SITE WRITTEN TOMORROW DEFAULTS TO REFUSED. A write-side guard was added too, since the twelve DefaultPath sites would have OVERWRITTEN her file without ever naming Delete. THE REDIRECT IS THE LOAD-BEARING LAYER and the guard is the second line: some sites call their own SafeDelete which invokes File.Delete DIRECTLY and never enters SaveSystem, so no guard could catch them. THE TRAP bd986 NEARLY WALKED INTO, worse than the bug: their first instinct was 'any argv flag containing probe means diagnostic' - and -phantomprobe IS THE FLAG HER OWN LAUNCHER PASSES, so her genuine progress would have been redirected to a temp directory and lost a SECOND way, through the fix, silently until her next launch. Excluded by name with the reason in the source. Assertions that moved (#1013), not the exit code: run recognised as diagnostic; DefaultPath outside LiveRoot; the zero-argument Delete() all ten sites make cannot reach the live root; a live path SURVIVES an unauthorised Delete AND DIES on playerInitiated:true (the discriminating pair); a live path is not overwritten by Save() from a diagnostic run. || MERGED 2026-08-26T22:04:57 at d34354f; her save.json still f7eebc9b after the merge, verified again. Freeze lifted wave-wide.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] WAVE RULE: a GOOD IDEA copied without its precondition spreads faster than a bug. A bug hurts and stops; a good idea does not hurt, so nothing stops it.
tasks.note: sp977's observation on why the save-deleting Delete() call reached seven probes. ALL SIX PROBES CARRY THE SAME COMMENT: 'the build she plays has no save.json - boot the state she actually boots.' The reasoning was DELIBERATE and CORRECT ABOUT DETERMINISM; it simply did not know that the editor and her build share one persistentDataPath. So it was copied as a good idea, comment and all, into every new probe - and each copy was written by someone doing the right thing for the right stated reason. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY FIX: removing the calls does not stop it coming back, because the next person will copy the comment again for the same good reason. The guard is what stops it - something that FAILS when the live save path is the target - not the deletion of the current instances. GENERAL FORM: when a pattern appears in N places with the same justification attached, do not treat it as N mistakes; find the precondition the justification assumes and check whether it holds. If it does not, the justification is what needs fixing, and the instances are downstream.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] WAVE RULE: an assertion only covers the paths someone has actually tried to walk. A corridor nobody had traversed had never been measured.
tasks.note: sp977 on #1033. Their #987 work genuinely covered routes, doorways and NPC cells - real coverage, honestly asserted. But the exam corridor was not in it, because until something was built that WALKS down a corridor, nobody had asked whether it could be walked. Measured the moment they did: the corridor spans z 2.40..4.24, medicine lockers take 3.89..4.23 and chairs+bins took 2.63..3.07, leaving A 0.82 m BAND FOR A 0.60 m BODY - one viable lane at z 3.5 with 0.09 m either side. That is not a lane, it is a coincidence, and it sat next to green assertions because no test had a reason to traverse it. GENERAL FORM: coverage is bounded by the ACTIONS anyone has modelled, not by the space that exists. When a new capability appears (walking, reaching, seeing from a new angle), the existing guards do not extend to it - they were never about it. THE FIX SHAPE MATTERS TOO AND IS #1017 AGAIN: sp977 moved the furniture 0.25 m rather than threading the route through the single gap, because A SINGLE-LANE CORRIDOR IS A DEFECT IN THE CORRIDOR, NOT A CONSTRAINT ON THE ROUTE. Threading it would have been carving the exception instead of fixing the predicate.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] WAVE RULE: do not read someone else's exit status through a pipe as if it were the command's own. Judge by the log's completion marker, not by $?.
tasks.note: THREE TIMES IN ONE DAY, each self-reported before anyone asked: sp977 piped a suite runner into `tail` and read TAIL's status, reporting 'the runner exits 0 with a failing guard' - false, run-all.sh exits 1 correctly; bd986 used PIPESTATUS in zsh and got an empty value, and declined to write a number they had not measured; bd986 again piped through `grep -v`, it matched nothing, and they read grep's status as the wrapper's. bd986's diagnosis is the rule: 'it is not a personal slip three times, it is the shell doing exactly what it promises and us asking the wrong process.' THE DEFENCE IS ALREADY IN THE REPO: unity-run.sh judges by the presence of the expected completion line rather than by an exit code, for exactly this reason - the same discipline applies when anyone hand-rolls a pipeline. Note the third instance happened AFTER the first two were known, which is the argument for writing it down rather than remembering it.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] Make M4aSelfTest explain ITSELF: two or three lines saying why it uses temporaryCachePath and what happens if you do not, naming #1040.
tasks.note: bd986's proposal, approved. THE ROOT NOBODY HAD FIXED: the wrong shape carried a plausible comment ('the build she plays has no save.json - boot the state she actually boots') and the right shape carried NO EXPLANATION AT ALL, so it read as an arbitrary choice and nobody copied it - while six probes copied the confident wrong one. This is #1016's other half: that ticket removed the wrong lines from the repo; this makes the right line carry its own reason. Together they are one rule - leave no wrong line to copy, and make the right line explain why it is right. Had the explanation been there, the direction of propagation would have been reversed. || MERGED 2026-08-26T22:06:30. ONE FILE, ELEVEN LINES ADDED AND ZERO REMOVED - pure comment, no executable change, and deliberately NOT verified by a Unity run because it changes nothing runnable and the device belonged to the user's top priority. The comment names #1040 and says three things: that companyName and productName are both AnimalHospital so the editor, sweeps, captures and HER BUILD share one directory; that eleven suites and seven probes destroyed her progress through that door today; and the line that matters most - IF YOU ARE WRITING A NEW SUITE THAT TOUCHES SAVES, COPY THIS LINE, NOT THAT COMMENT. That sentence is aimed at the moment the next person will actually be in, which is precisely the moment the six probes copied the wrong comment. bd986's closing formulation is the keeper: EXPLANATION IS WHAT MAKES A PATTERN COPYABLE, AND CORRECTNESS ON ITS OWN IS NOT.

tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] WAVE RULE: a standard applied strictly where it is cheap and leniently where it is expensive is not a standard. Check the cases where holding it costs YOU something.
tasks.note: sp977 caught this on themselves within an hour of setting the standard. tasks.desc: [animal-hospital] WAVE RULE: eliminating one candidate only helps if the candidate LIST was complete. On a two-item list, elimination turns into proof - and a precondition check that narrows an incomplete list makes you confidently wrong.
tasks.note: bd986, at the last verification of the cut. Their liquid probe read 0.0008mm and they were about to report HeldLiquid dead. THE THIRD CANDIDATE WAS NOT ON THE LIST: my own assertion encodes the wrong physics. HeldLiquid:82 is a = (v - _prevVel)/dt, so THE SPRING IS DRIVEN BY ACCELERATION - constant walking means zero drive, forced by the maths and documented in an979's comment. Their test gave the player 10 warm-up frames to REACH constant velocity and then measured 45 frames: it measured exactly the interval where a correct implementation MUST do nothing, and reported that silence as a defect. Real liquid behaves the same - a cup carried at constant speed is flat and surges when you start, stop or turn - and an979's header says so in those words, which bd986 had read. THEIR OWN FORMULATION IS THE RULE: 'the precondition check did not save me; reading the source AFTER the precondition passed is what saved me.' Fixed by sampling the TRANSITIONS - 45 frames from the moment W is pressed and 45 from the moment it is released, with standing still kept as a control that must read zero. Which is also what she will actually see: a ten-year-old walks and stops and turns, she does not cross a corridor at constant velocity.

tasks.desc: read-screen resolves TASK_COMPLETION_UNKNOWN when no reply is coming — read DEEP, grep SINGLE tokens, and beware the other end probing with the same ones.
tasks.note: sp977 2026-08-27 found the procedure: their inject 9e11d6c1 came back TASK_COMPLETION_UNKNOWN with no reply due (they had said none was needed), so the content-side proof everyone had been relying on could never arrive. `telepty read-screen orchestrator --lines 120` then grep a distinctive phrase; they found their own sentences and did not re-send. All three TASK_COMPLETION_UNKNOWN events tonight were resolved by noticing content in a REPLY, which only works when a reply is coming - this closes the case where one is not. || ORCHESTRATOR RE-MEASURED IT AND IT NEEDS A QUALIFIER THEY DID NOT HAVE. Verified: the command form is real (`telepty read-screen <id[@host]> [--lines N]`) and the orchestrator's session id is literally `orchestrator` (NOT aigentry-orchestrator, which returns 'not found' - my first attempt aimed at the wrong id and returned a clean 0 that meant nothing). But run against a live orchestrator MID-TURN, `--lines 200` came back 185 lines of spinner frames with ZERO conversation content: hits for '9e11d6c1', 'read-screen', 'LAST ONE' and 'measurable' were all 0 for a message that had certainly arrived. THE SCREEN IS A LIVE RENDER, NOT A LOG. So: hit => delivered, do not re-send. MISS => UNKNOWN, and re-sending on that basis is the duplicate the procedure exists to prevent. Same shape as everything else tonight - a clean zero with two meanings - and found only by running it with a positive control instead of adopting it. || sp977 FOUND TWO FAILURE MODES BY USING IT WITHIN FIVE MINUTES, and handed me the caveated version rather than the clean one. (1) DEPTH: --lines 200 gave them 22KB and none of their message, --lines 3000 gave 41KB and some. It fails SILENTLY TOWARD NOT-DELIVERED and they nearly reported a lost message on it. Orchestrator re-measured on its own buffer: 200 lines = 2,071 bytes / 28 non-spinner lines; 800 = 5,527 / 103; 3000 = 43,088 / 430. A shallow read sees about 6% of what a deep one does - so depth is not a tuning knob, and my earlier 'a miss proves nothing' was the same phenomenon seen without its mechanism. (2) PROBE COLLISION - the instrument seeing another instrument: grepping my screen for tokens from their message, they found 9e11d6c1 and 'measurable', and the context was MY OWN for-loop probing for those exact tokens. When both ends check delivery with the same distinctive tokens, each finds the other's grep and reads it as arrival - A FALSE POSITIVE MANUFACTURED OUT OF THE CHECK ITSELF. Also: multi-word phrases break across terminal line wrapping ('measurable' matched, 'makes it measurable' did not, same buffer). Grep single tokens. || AND THE RESOLUTION BEAT THE CHECK: my probe searched for 'LAST ONE' and 'measurable', phrases existing ONLY in the body of the message whose delivery was in question, so I could not have built that grep without having received it. Delivery was proven not by finding their text on my screen but BY OBSERVING THAT I WAS LOOKING FOR THEIR TEXT. Property, not identifier, one more time - and this time the property was someone else's behaviour rather than a file's contents. || 2026-09-06: codified as Rule 44 in docs/rules.md (orchestrator, own domain); one condensed AGENTS.md checklist row for 41-44.

tasks.desc: Stop-hook / every node child dies with MODULE_NOT_FOUND: NODE_OPTIONS --require points at a $TMPDIR shim macOS purged mid-session. Fixed by restoring the file verbatim; needs a permanent guard.
tasks.note: DIAGNOSED AND WORKED AROUND 2026-08-30. SYMPTOM: 4 stop hooks failed, and so did `npm test`, `telepty`, `node -p` - anything spawning node from this session - with Cannot find module '/var/folders/.../T/cmux-claude-node-options/restore-node-options.cjs', requireStack ['internal/preload']. MECHANISM, each step measured: cmux's wrapper (/Applications/cmux.app/Contents/Resources/bin/cmux-claude-wrapper, ensure_node_options_restore_module at :628) writes that shim under $TMPDIR and exports NODE_OPTIONS='--require=<shim> --max-old-space-size=4096' into the claude process. The claude process here (pid 6984) started 2026-08-16, so its env is FROZEN with that path. The shim's directory still exists but is EMPTY, and its mtime is 2026-08-28 03:38 - the timestamp of the deletion. macOS purges $TMPDIR files that go untouched for ~3 days; the wrapper only recreates the shim at CLAUDE LAUNCH, so a session that outlives the purge keeps a --require pointing at nothing. Node applies --require BEFORE running anything, so every child dies at preload - the parent survives because it loaded the module 14 days ago. FIX APPLIED: recreated the file byte-for-byte from the wrapper's own heredoc (it restores CMUX_ORIGINAL_NODE_OPTIONS for grandchildren, or deletes NODE_OPTIONS when CMUX_ORIGINAL_NODE_OPTIONS_PRESENT=0, which is this env). Verified: `node -e` now runs with NODE_OPTIONS inherited and reports undefined in the child - i.e. the shim is doing its job - and telepty lists 7 sessions again. Copying the content rather than writing a no-op matters: a no-op would have left NODE_OPTIONS set for every grandchild, which is exactly what cmux wrote the shim to prevent. PERMANENT FIX IS CMUX'S, upstream: either put the shim somewhere the OS does not sweep (~/Library/Application Support/cmux) or have the wrapper touch/recreate it periodically. Any long-lived session is affected, not just this one - it is a 3-day fuse on every claude launched through cmux. WORKAROUND FOR OTHERS MEANWHILE: prefix `NODE_OPTIONS= ` on node commands, which is what I did for hours today without diagnosing the cause - a workaround applied often enough to stop looking like a symptom. | dispatched 2026-09-05T12:43:15Z sid=mr1075-mr1075-node-options-shim ref=2026-09-05-mr1075-node-options-shim.md track=mr1075 cli=claude/claude-fable-5-1[1m] by=explicit || HOLD 2026-09-05 (shared/b4dce01b…): step 0f in src/reconciler/cli.ts (the .sh is an exec shim); canonical shim content = wrapper heredoc :636-643 (340 B, sha 7cfe713c…, byte-equal to the live shim; cmux 0.64.20 build 100). tasks.desc: An inject can be ENQUEUED to a worker's mailbox and never delivered as a turn — ps981 lost a full reply for 32 minutes, and every 'no answer = they are busy' inference depends on that path.
tasks.note: ps981 reported 2026-08-31: my 00:43:29 reply never reached their conversation. They found it only by reading ~/.aigentry/mailbox/<sid>/inbox.jsonl after the daemon fired TASK_COMPLETION_UNKNOWN on eba79d34 at 01:15:33. The monitor was wrong in the direction it named - the inject WAS consumed and answered in full - while pointing at a real anomaly running the other way. ORCHESTRATOR INSPECTED THE MAILBOX AND FOUND ITS EXACT LIMIT: records carry msg_id, from, to, payload, created_at and ATTEMPT, and NO delivered/consumed field. So the mailbox proves ENQUEUE, not DELIVERY, and the gap between enqueue and turn-delivery is unobserved by anything we have. That is a THIRD delivery check with a third failure mode, alongside #1060's read-screen (a hit proves delivery, a miss proves nothing) and the daemon's TASK_COMPLETION_UNKNOWN (wrong in both directions). None of the three answers 'did this become a turn'. || INCIDENTAL: the newest mailbox entry at 01:50:15 was a RESUME nudge sent under the identity 'orchestrator' that I DID NOT SEND ('your last turn was cut mid-response by host sleep'). Something automated - dispatch-tracker or the reconcile tick - injects as the orchestrator. Worth knowing before attributing an unexplained worker turn to myself. || ps981 WENT LOOKING FOR A DISCRIMINATOR AND FOUND MOSTLY BAD NEWS, which is the useful half. NO STRUCTURAL TELL: every record carries the same key set (attempt, created_at, from, msg_id, payload, to) - no delivered, no consumed, and no source/agent/origin - msg_id has the same shape for both (orchestrator:<epoch_ms>:<8hex>), and attempt is 0 everywhere. FROM THE RECEIVING SIDE AN AUTOMATION INJECT UNDER MY NAME IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ME BY ENVELOPE. Language fails too and they checked before assuming: 15 of my messages to them open in Korean and 25 do not, so 'Korean means human' would have been comfortable and wrong. THE ONE TELL, verified independently by the orchestrator: the automation sends a FIXED TEMPLATE. Hashing every orchestrator-sent payload in their inbox: 43 sent, 41 unique, EXACTLY ONE repeated - sha256 prefix 02a96e183a8e, three times, 23:32:52 / 01:50:15 / 02:09:23. So a payload repeating byte-for-byte under from=orchestrator is automation, because in 40 unique messages I never sent the same text twice. ITS LIMIT, stated by them: it only fires on the SECOND occurrence, so a new template gets one free impersonation - the 23:32:52 one was undetectable and they attributed it to me at the time. Byte count differs slightly, they say 305 and I measure 307; naming it rather than picking one. AND I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE COUNT: I reported the 01:50:15 nudge as the incident; there were three. I read the newest record and called it the event. || THEIR TIMER CLAIM IS FALSIFIED, and I re-measured rather than adopting it (Rule 39). They inferred TASK_COMPLETION_UNKNOWN runs on a ~32-minute timer from two samples, 1975.6s and 1936.1s. Counting every alert in this session's transcript: 866 alerts, elapsed_since_inject from 15.4s to 35,327.6s (9.8 hours), median 673.2s, and ONLY 4 OF 866 fall in the 1900-2000s band. Their two samples landed near each other by coincidence. WHAT SURVIVES IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: consumption=not_established is reported on all 866 regardless of whether the message was consumed, and it fails toward 'no answer' - the direction that makes a session resend or sit idle. The mechanism is not a timer; the bias is real. || 305 vs 307 SETTLED WITHOUT EITHER SIDE GIVING WAY, and verified independently: the payload is 305 CHARACTERS and 307 UTF-8 BYTES, containing exactly one non-ASCII character - U+2014 EM DASH at index 114, which is 3 bytes and 1 character, so the gap is exactly +2. ps981 counted characters and called them bytes; I counted bytes. The record reads '305 characters / 307 bytes' rather than choosing, and the tell is unaffected because it is a sha256 identity. A DISAGREEMENT WHERE BOTH NUMBERS WERE RIGHT AND MEASURED DIFFERENT THINGS - worth keeping as the counter-example to the night's usual shape, where a disagreement meant one side had not measured. The resolution came from naming the UNIT, not from re-counting. ps981 withdrew the timer claim on the same grounds I withdrew mine: n=2, and two points that land near each other are not a mechanism. Both of us read the most recent record and called it the event - they on the nudge count, I on 01:50:15. || THE TELL FIRED IN PRODUCTION 2026-08-31 03:33:27 and ps981 hashed rather than eyeballed: sha256 02a96e183a8e, 305 characters - fourth occurrence, verdict AUTOMATION. AND ITS PREMISE IS FALSE, which is new: the template asserts 'your last turn was cut mid-response by host sleep' when their last turn COMPLETED and reached me (I answered it). So it does not merely arrive under my name, it asserts a non-event AND instructs the receiver to re-read the dispatch and resume work. Had they obeyed they would have restarted a merged ticket while I was telling them to hold. Concrete cost, not theoretical. || ORCHESTRATOR TRACED THE SENDER: src/reconciler/cli.ts:652 RESUME_MSG, injected at :659 with `--from $ORCH_SID`. THE IMPERSONATION IS DELIBERATE AND DOCUMENTED AT :575 - 'a reconciler-named sender would be a non-orch<->non-orch peer inject, which session-comms-auditor.sh classifies out-of-policy and HOLDs to the orchestrator - one operator page per recovery.' So this is a designed trade-off, not an oversight, and renaming the sender is not the fix. It is bounded by a LATCH (one per occurrence, cleared only by seeing the sid on another surface) and a RATE CAP (default 3/sid/hour). THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THE CLASSIFIER, and it is tonight's shape again: A SESSION INSTRUCTED TO HOLD AND A SESSION KILLED MID-RESPONSE PRODUCE THE SAME OBSERVATION - telemetry silence - so the nudge cannot tell 'correctly idle' from 'cut', and it resolves toward 'cut' and tells the worker to resume. || FOURTH CONFIRMATION PATH KILLED: THE MAILBOX DOES NOT RETAIN. ps981 went to count occurrences and found inbox.jsonl holding TWO records with no rotation file beside it; I re-measured minutes later and found FOUR, earliest 03:16:45 - the 43 records I hashed at 02:xx are gone. So the byte-identical tell is only usable by someone who RETAINED the earlier payloads, and ABSENCE FROM A MAILBOX PROVES NOTHING - not consumed, not never-arrived. All four paths now fail: read-screen (hit only), the daemon alarm (both directions), the mailbox (enqueue only, and now: no history). CONSEQUENCE ALREADY TAKEN: the hash lives in this ticket because it will not survive in the mailbox - 02a96e183a8e / 305 characters / 307 UTF-8 bytes is the whole tell and #1079 is the only place it persists. || RETRACTED, MY ERROR: I wrote that state/sleep-resume.json does not exist and therefore resumeLatchClear() returns early. I LOOKED ONE DIRECTORY TOO HIGH. cli.ts:65 is `STATE_DIR = env.DISPATCH_STATE_DIR || path.join(REPO_DIR, "state/dispatch")`, DISPATCH_STATE_DIR is unset here, and the file EXISTS at state/dispatch/sleep-resume.json, 397 bytes, mtime 04:41:29 - actively written. ps981 hit the same absent answer at two wrong paths first and said that stopping there would have CONFIRMED my finding instead of correcting it. Same shape as the working-tree census. That sentence is removed from this ticket rather than left with a correction beside it.

completed.desc: Polyrepo + universalized service ecosystem 베스트 프랙티스 조사 — DONE. 10 사례 (LangChain/HF/MCP/Grafana/HashiCorp/googleapis/Buf BSR/Confluent SR/k8s/Neovim) + 47 citations.
